throughput_single_line.quote: Straight grate: 'Capacities ranging from 0.6 MTPA to 9 MTPA in a single system'; grate-kiln: 'Capacities ranging from 3 MTPA to 7 MTPA in a single system'
throughput_single_line.note: Guess 125 t/h = about 1.0 Mt/yr at 8000 h, i.e. a small single line; typical modern lines are 3-7 Mt/yr (375-875 t/h).

electricity_vendor.quote: 'Approx. 50 kWh/ton power consumption' (straight grate column) and 'Approx. 42 kWh/ton power consumption' (grate-kiln column)
electricity_vendor.note: Guess 8 MW / 125 t/h = 64 kWh/t; about 30-50 % above the vendor figure. Column assignment read from PDF layout.

electricity_EU_plants.unit: MJ electric per t pellets (= 15-27.5 kWh/t)
electricity_EU_plants.quote: Table 4.1 'Input/output data from three pellet plant sites in the EU-25': Electricity MJ/t 54 - 99
electricity_EU_plants.note: Guess of 64 kWh/t is 2-4x the EU plant range.

ore_per_t_pellets.unit: kg iron ore (concentrate) per t pellets
ore_per_t_pellets.quote: Table 4.1: Iron ore kg/t 935 - 965; Pellets kg/t 1000
ore_per_t_pellets.note: Guess 1.5 t ore per t pellets is wrong by about +55 %; pelletizing gains mass by binder/flux and (for magnetite) oxidation. 1.5 would only apply if 'ore' means run-of-mine before beneficiation, which is a different plant.

bentonite.note: Other fluxes: olivine 0-27.6, limestone 0-5, dolomite 0-13.5 kg/t.

heat_fuel.quote: 'Gross energy consumption of the above-mentioned pelletisation plant is approximately 1.4 GJ/t pellet ... About 0.7 GJ/t pellet is supplied by means of heat recuperation, whereas approximately 0.7 GJ/t pellet is introduced by means of fuel.' Table 4.1 Swedish magnetite plants: Coal 223 MJ/t, Oil 43 - 186 MJ/t
heat_fuel.note: Low end = magnetite (exothermic oxidation), high end = hematite. Registry guess had no heat term.

footprint.note: No citable site dimensions found for a stated capacity.

throughput.unit: t DRI/h for a 1.6 Mt/yr module
throughput.note: Guess 125 t/h = 1.0 Mt/yr is a valid smaller module. Wikipedia 'Direct reduction' (IEA ETSAP 2010 table) gives Midrex capacity 400 to 1700 kt/year; Midrex 2021 operations summary reports 114 t/h (OEMK module 1) and 226 t/h (Jindal Shadeed).

hydrogen_consumption.unit: kg H2 per t DRI (650 Nm3/t)
hydrogen_consumption.note: Exact match. Vogl et al. 2018 model: '51 kg of hydrogen is needed per tonne of steel output' without losses (https://xylenepower.com/Assessment%20of%20hydrogen%20direct%20reduction%20for%20fossil-free%20steelmaking.pdf).

pellets_per_t_liquid_steel.unit: kg iron ore pellets per t liquid steel (100 % HBI charge to EAF)
pellets_per_t_liquid_steel.quote: 'For continuous operation on 100% HBI, the production of one tonne of steel requires 1504 kg of iron ore pellets.'
pellets_per_t_liquid_steel.note: This is per tonne of STEEL, not per tonne of sponge iron. A sourced pellets-per-tonne-DRI ratio (the 1.43 guess) was NOT found; 1.43 is consistent with Fe2O3 stoichiometry but unsourced.

electricity.unit: kWh electric per t DRI (natural-gas Midrex, excludes hydrogen production and gas heating)
electricity.quote: ArcelorMittal Hamburg: 'Its annual average electricity consumption was the lowest of all MIDREX Plants at 82 kWh per ton.' Wikipedia 'Direct reduction' table (IEA ETSAP 2010): Midrex 'Electricity requirement (kWh/t)' 135.4 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Direct_reduction)
electricity.note: Guess 12 MW / 125 t/h = 96 kWh/t sits inside the range. An all-electric H2 gas heater would add to this; not separately sourced.

system_energy_H2_route.unit: MWh electric per t liquid steel (electrolyser + shaft + EAF)
system_energy_H2_route.quote: 'hydrogen direct reduction steelmaking needs 3.48 MWh of electricity per tonne of liquid steel, mainly for the electrolyser hydrogen production'

tower_height.quote: 'capable of producing two million tons of hot-briquetted iron per year ... its 137-meter-high reduction tower'
tower_height.note: Guess 120 m is close (-12 %), and that for a plant twice the guessed capacity. Furnace inner diameter 7.15 m per search summary of the same Primetals pages (not re-read).

specific_electricity.quote: 'As of 2022, commercial electrolysis requires around 53 kWh of electricity to produce one kg of hydrogen'
specific_electricity.note: 100 MW / 53 kWh/kg = 1.89 t H2/h; guess 1.9 t/h confirmed.

water_stoichiometric.quote: 'Per chemistry fundamentals, 9 liters (L) of water are required to produce 1 kilogram (kg) of hydrogen via electrolysis.'

water_total.unit: L water per kg H2 including purification and cooling

water_total.note: Guess of 9 t/t is the reaction minimum only; real raw-water intake is 2-3x that.

footprint.unit: hectares per 1 GW plant (= 0.8-1.7 ha per 100 MW)

footprint.note: Guess 150x100 m = 1.5 ha per 100 MW is inside the range (linear scaling from GW size is my assumption).

largest_plant.quote: 'the largest is a 150 MW alkaline facility in Ningxia, China, with a capacity up to 23,000 tonnes per year'

It consumes 530 kWh/t ... liquid steel for the EAF'; Vogl et al.: 'producing steel in the EAF from scrap requires less energy (0.667 MWh/tLS) than from pure DRI (0.753 MWh/tLS)' (https://xylenepower.com/Assessment%20of%20hydrogen%20direct%20reduction%20for%20fossil-free%20steelmaking.pdf)
electricity_DRI_charge.note: Guess 500 kWh/t with DRI charge is low: 530 is best practice at 60 % DRI, about 750 for 100 % cold DRI/HBI (model value). LBNL also: DRI raises EAF electricity 'by 40-120 kWh/t liquid steel'.
